Goal: I can prove a line parallel to one side divides the others proportionally, and its converse.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Side-Splitter Theorem: if a line parallel to one side of a triangle crosses the other two sides, it divides them proportionally. Converse: if a line divides two sides proportionally, it is parallel to the third side.

In triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC (D on AB, E on AC): AD/DB = AE/EC. Proof idea: the dilation about A that maps D to B maps line DE to the parallel line through B, which is BC, so E maps to C and AB/AD = AC/AE.

Equally spaced parallel lines, like the lines on notebook paper, cut any slanted segment into equal parts.
